entries.title: Report Builder: filter and sort by reviewer recommendation
entries.summary: In a Sessions report, **Reviewer recommendation** (Accept, Decline or Alternate) and **Reviewer recommendation note** are now under **Reviews** in the Fields panel. They filter and sort, and on one row per session they count each recommendation, so a report can list every session a reviewer marked Alternate.

where.path: Reports → Report Builder → Fields → Reviews → Reviewer recommendation

entries.use_case: Program teams that triage with reviewer recommendations can pull Accept, Decline and Alternate straight into a report, count them per session and filter to the Alternates, instead of building a rubric question to copy the call.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says the Recommendation column in Report Builder is blank, or asks how to report on reviewers' Accept / Decline / Alternate calls.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using reviewer recommendations (the Accept / Decline / Alternate feature on a review plan round) who also uses Report Builder.
internal.staff_path: Reports → Report Builder → add a Reviews column → Reviewer recommendation
internal.gotchas: Reads the round's Recommendation feature, not a rubric question labelled 'Recommendation'. A rubric workaround question still shows in its own column. A recommendation the reviewer removed stops showing.
internal.talk_track: If your reviewers recommend Accept, Decline or Alternate in a round, those calls are now report columns you can filter and count.

entries.title: Campaign preview counts only the contacts you picked
entries.summary: An email campaign that holds hand-picked contacts (one copied or duplicated with its picked contacts) now previews and counts exactly those contacts on **Preview as…**, the same people it sends to, instead of everyone in the event. When **Review** on a Send Email can't build a preview, the reason the server gave is shown with the error.

where.path: Communications → Email Campaigns → campaign → Preview

entries.use_case: The preview and count now match who will actually get a duplicated hand-picked campaign, so organizers can trust the number before they send.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that a duplicated campaign's preview listed far more people than it was sent to, or that Review failed with no reason.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who send from selected records and duplicate those campaigns.
internal.staff_path: Event → Communications → Email Campaigns → open campaign → Preview
internal.gotchas: Sending was always correct; only the preview list and count were wrong.

entries.title: Speakers who sign in at the organizer login are pointed to their portal
entries.summary: A speaker, submitter or reviewer who signs in at the organizer login with no organization to open no longer hits a bare **No organizations found**. The page explains that their drafts and submissions are in the event's portal, reached from the event's email or the submission form, shows the email they are signed in with, and offers **Sign out**.

where.path: Organizer login → home page, signed in without an organization

entries.use_case: Speakers who land in the wrong place now see where to go, which saves a support email for the organizer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer forwards a speaker's 'No organizations found' screenshot.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer with external submitters or speakers.
internal.staff_path: Sign in at the admin login as a contact with no organization access
internal.gotchas: The fix is the explanation; the person still has to open the portal link from the event's email or submission form.

entries.title: Link preview text for a Site
entries.summary: The Site builder has a **Link preview** setting under **Social share image**: the text shown under the Site's name when its link is pasted into Slack, LinkedIn or Teams (up to 300 characters), with a preview card beside it. Left empty, the card uses the landing **Subtitle** as before.

where.path: Sites → open a Site → Settings → Site → Link preview

entries.use_case: Organizers can write the text a shared Site link shows without changing the subtitle visitors see on the landing page.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to change the text Slack or LinkedIn shows for their Site link.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who share Awards or program Site links on social or in Slack.
internal.staff_path: Org → Sites → Site → Settings → Site → Link preview
internal.gotchas: Takes effect after Publish. Slack and LinkedIn cache previews of links they have already seen for a while.

entries.title: SSO-only Sites publish without opening Login / SSO first
entries.summary: A Site with **SSO Login** as its only sign-in method could refuse to publish with **Select at least one identity provider or disable SSO login** after a reload, unless you opened **Login / SSO** first. **Publish** now checks the identity providers linked to the Site, so a duplicated SSO-only Site publishes straight away.

where.path: Sites → Site builder → Publish

entries.use_case: Organizers who duplicate an SSO-only Site for a new season can publish it without a confusing error.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports the identity-provider error on publish although SSO is set up.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with SSO-only Sites.
internal.staff_path: Org → Sites → Site → Publish
internal.gotchas: The error is still correct when no provider is linked to the Site.

entries.title: Adding a new speaker works again on events with Gleanin
entries.summary: On events with Gleanin connected, adding a **new** contact to a session (the **Add contact** panel) failed with **Request failed**. It works again; adding an existing contact was not affected.

where.path: Program → Sessions → session → Participants → Add

entries.use_case: Organizers on Gleanin-connected events can add brand-new speakers to sessions again.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Gleanin customer reported 'Request failed' adding a speaker in mid-November.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Gleanin connected.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Sessions → session → Participants → Add → new contact
internal.gotchas: Broke with the 2026-11-15 release; fixed in the next deploy.

entries.title: Screener: persona scores show on the Reviews tab and Ratings column, and runs no longer stall
entries.summary: Screener persona scores on dropdown questions now appear on a session's **Reviews** tab, in the **Ratings: <plan>** column and in round averages, the same as on the plan. Personas also finish rounds whose dropdown options were saved with an extra space (such as " Strong"), so those submissions no longer stay pending.

where.path: Review plans → [plan] → Evaluators → Personas → Run personas; session → Reviews tab; Program → View All → Ratings: [plan] column

entries.use_case: Program teams that use Screener personas can rank submissions on one consistent score: persona scores now count everywhere human scores do, and a run reviews every assigned submission instead of leaving a few pending.

cs_action.note: Customers whose persona runs stopped short (progress below 100%) should click Run personas once more; the remaining submissions complete. Persona scores that showed '-' now show values with no re-run needed (scores are computed when the page loads). US only: 10 plans had persona dropdown answers; EU had none.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says persona scores show on the plan but not on the session's Reviews tab or the Ratings column, round averages ignore personas, or Run personas stays below 100% on the same submissions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running Screener personas on a review plan round with dropdown scorecard questions.
internal.staff_path: Event → Review plans → [plan] → Evaluators → Personas (progress, Run personas); Program → View All with the Ratings: [plan] column; session pop-out → Reviews tab
internal.gotchas: Scores already saved are fixed on read, with nothing to backfill. Submissions a persona never finished need one more Run personas. Option labels are still saved as typed; matching now ignores case and extra spaces.
internal.talk_track: Screener's persona scores now count everywhere your human reviewers' scores do, and if a persona run stopped short before, run it once more and it will finish.

entries.title: Market Radar: see similar events on the event dashboard and track them in Recon
entries.summary: A new **Market Radar** card on the event dashboard (**Today** tab) shows the events most similar to yours — how close they are, which topics they cover that yours doesn't, and how many are still upcoming. Opening **Market Radar** from the dashboard leads to a full page where each similar event shows its organizer, dates, location, summary, topics, and official agenda. From any card, **Track in Recon** creates a Recon event and starts its first read; the card then shows **Reading…**, **Read** (with a link to the comparison), or a retry option. The Recon external-event page opens its **Intelligence** tab automatically when the link includes a `?compareWith` parameter.

where.path: Event → Today (dashboard) → Market Radar card; Event → Market Radar page

entries.use_case: An event organizer can instantly see which competing or adjacent events are most similar to theirs, spot topic gaps in their own program, and start monitoring a rival event's agenda — all without leaving Sessionboard. This is especially useful during the call-for-speakers phase when understanding the competitive landscape helps sharpen the program.

cs_action.note: The UI depends on a companion API PR (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5488). The radar card stays hidden until the API returns an analysis and until at least one similar event with a verified agenda exists. Tracking in Recon also requires the API PR to be deployed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to benchmark their program against competing events, or when they are in the call-for-speakers phase and want to identify topic gaps.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Speaker Prospects (beta) enabled who want competitive intelligence on similar events.
internal.staff_path: Event → Today → Market Radar card (hidden without Speaker Prospects or without an analysis from the API)
internal.gotchas: The card is hidden if Speaker Prospects is not enabled or if the API has not yet returned a similar-events analysis. Only events with a verified agenda appear. Polling for Recon read status stops automatically after 20 minutes. The Recon event list is capped at 200 events, but re-tracking is idempotent.
internal.talk_track: Market Radar shows you the events most similar to yours, highlights topics they cover that you don't, and lets you track their agendas in Recon for a live comparison — all from your event dashboard.

draft.docs_gap: The Event Dashboard guide should document the Market Radar card (when it appears, what it shows, and how to navigate to the full Market Radar page), and a new Market Radar guide should cover the full page, the Track in Recon flow, read statuses, and the ?compareWith deep-link into the Recon Intelligence tab.
draft.why_use_it: Market Radar surfaces the events most similar to yours so you can understand the competitive landscape without manual research. The dashboard card gives you a quick read on proximity, topic overlap and upcoming events; the full Market Radar page lets you dig into each event's agenda, organizer and topics it covers that yours doesn't. Tracking an event in Recon kicks off an automated agenda read and links directly to a side-by-side comparison, so you always know what the field is programming.

entries.title: Webinar Follow-ups panel, AI-triggered drafts on arrival, and Results email notification switch
entries.summary: A new **Follow-ups** panel appears at the top of a webinar's page in the Marketing workspace, surfacing AI-suggested actions (registered / came / questions) from the post-webinar digest — each with **Apply** / **Skip** and **Apply all** controls, plus a record of who applied each item and when. Opening the webinar with `?digest=1&draft=1` automatically starts clip-pack generation and recap drafts once, then drops the flag so a reload does not repeat. A new **Results and follow-ups** toggle in **Account settings → Emails from Sessionboard** lets each user opt out of the results email for Marketing webinars.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the webinar digest; then Marketing → Events → [webinar page]

where.path: Marketing → Events → [webinar] → Follow-ups panel

entries.use_case: After a webinar ends, the Follow-ups panel surfaces AI-generated action items — such as updating registration counts or drafting follow-up content — so the team can act on them in one place without hunting through reports. The Results email switch lets individual users control whether they receive the post-webinar results digest for Marketing events.

cs_action.note: The Follow-ups panel is hidden when the API returns available: false — it is not self-serve. CS must enable the webinar digest feature for the org before customers see the panel.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running regular webinars asks for a post-event workflow or wants to streamline follow-up content creation after each webinar.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing customers who run webinars and want a guided post-webinar action workflow.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Events → [webinar page] — panel appears at top when digest is available; Account settings → Emails from Sessionboard → Results and follow-ups for the email switch.
internal.gotchas: The panel is hidden entirely when the API returns available: false, so customers on older API versions or without the feature enabled will not see it. The ?digest=1&draft=1 flag triggers clip and recap generation only once — a page reload will not repeat it. The Results email switch requires the web-api PR #5489 to be deployed; on an older API the section is simply absent from Account settings.
internal.talk_track: After your webinar wraps, the Follow-ups panel gives your team a checklist of AI-suggested next steps — approve them all at once or pick and choose — and automatically queues up clips and recap drafts so your content is ready to go.

draft.docs_gap: The results-email guide should document the new Follow-ups panel (location, Apply/Skip/Apply all controls, the applied-by record, and the ?digest=1 deep-link behaviour) and the Results and follow-ups toggle in Account settings → Emails from Sessionboard.
draft.why_use_it: The results email and Follow-ups panel give your team a structured post-webinar workflow: the digest arrives automatically after each webinar, and the Follow-ups panel translates it into discrete actions you can approve or skip directly on the webinar page. Opening the webinar from the digest link kicks off clip and recap drafts in the background, so content is ready to review without any manual steps. Each action records who applied it and when, giving the whole team visibility into what has already been handled.

entries.title: Surveys directory is now available on every event
entries.summary: The **Surveys** directory and editor are now accessible on every event without any feature flag or early-access gate. A "rolling out" placeholder message that previously appeared instead of the survey list has been removed.

where.path: Event → Surveys

entries.use_case: Any event team that tried to open Surveys and saw the "turning on" placeholder can now access the full Surveys directory and create or edit surveys immediately, with no action required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that their Surveys page shows a rollout placeholder or that surveys are inaccessible on a production event.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers — Surveys is now GA and on by default for every event.
internal.staff_path: Event → Surveys
internal.gotchas: The Learning overview still gates its unlock on enabled_features.includes('surveys'); that behaviour is unchanged. Demo mode events are also unchanged — Surveys remains off in demo mode.
internal.talk_track: Surveys are now live on every event. You can go straight to Event → Surveys to create and share feedback forms — no setup or support request needed.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that Surveys is now available on every event by default (GA) and that no early-access toggle is required.
draft.why_use_it: Surveys let you collect session, speaker, and event feedback directly inside Sessionboard, keeping responses alongside your program data. You can create surveys, share them with attendees, and review results without leaving the platform. Responses feed into your reporting alongside session and speaker records, making it easy to act on feedback after the event.

entries.title: Render all suggested clips for a recording in one click
entries.summary: A new **Render N suggested clips** button appears on the import detail page (**Media › History › [import]**) and on a recording's **Suggested clips** card. One click starts every pending suggested clip render — applying the brand kit (logo, captions, every kit size) — and shows a toast with the count kicked off. The button updates its count after each run and shows **"Every suggested clip is rendered."** when nothing remains. A note indicates how many recordings are still processing.

where.path: Marketing › Media › History › [import] — header; or Marketing › Media › [recording] › Suggested clips card

entries.use_case: Events with large recording libraries — such as a multi-day conference with 100+ sessions — can kick off every suggested clip render in a single click instead of triggering each one individually, saving hours of manual work when producing post-event content.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer with a large recording library asks how to speed up post-event content production or complains about the volume of clicks needed to render clips.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Media with Clips enabled who import recordings from multi-session events.
internal.staff_path: Marketing › Media › History › [import] or Marketing › Media › [recording] › Suggested clips
internal.gotchas: The button is hidden until the supporting web-api endpoint (render-suggested) is live; it fails quietly and stays hidden if the API is not yet deployed. Recordings still processing are counted and shown as a note rather than included in the render batch.
internal.talk_track: Instead of clicking through 200+ suggested clips one by one, you can now render your entire library of suggestions in a single click — the brand kit is applied automatically to every size.

draft.docs_gap: The media-library guide should document the Render N suggested clips button — where it appears, what it does (dry-run count, batch render with brand kit, all-rendered state, processing-recordings note), and that it requires the render-suggested API endpoint to be available.
draft.why_use_it: The Media library lets you turn session recordings into ready-to-share clips automatically, with your brand kit applied — logo, captions, and every aspect ratio. Suggested clips surface the most shareable moments from each recording so your team starts from the best material rather than scrubbing through hours of footage. Rendering all suggestions at once means your full clip library is ready to review and distribute as soon as the event wraps.

entries.title: Render all suggested clips in every aspect ratio with one action
entries.summary: Two new API endpoints — one for recordings and one for imported media — queue every suggested clip window across all supported aspect ratios (e.g. 9:16 and 16:9) in a single call, applying the event's brand kit with logo and captions. A **dryRun** option returns the count of clips that would be created before committing. Clips that already exist for a given window and size are skipped automatically.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable this endpoint; then POST /v1/orgs/:orgId/media/:mediaId/clips/render-suggested or /v1/orgs/:orgId/media/imports/:importId/render-suggested

where.path: Marketing → Media → Clips (via API or AI assistant)

entries.use_case: Events with dozens or hundreds of session recordings can generate branded clips in every required aspect ratio across all suggested windows in one step, instead of triggering each size individually. This is especially useful for post-event content teams who need 9:16 and 16:9 versions of every highlight ready for social distribution.

cs_action.note: This is an API/MCP-only surface in this PR; the UI button ships in a follow-on web-ui-v2 PR. Reach out to customers who have large recording libraries (50+ sessions) and are currently generating clips one at a time.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer with many recordings asks how to bulk-generate social clips or complains about the number of clicks needed to render clips in multiple sizes.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Marketing Clips with a significant volume of session recordings who need clips in multiple aspect ratios.
internal.staff_path: POST /v1/orgs/:orgId/media/:mediaId/clips/render-suggested or /v1/orgs/:orgId/media/imports/:importId/render-suggested — also available as MCP tools render_suggested_clips and render_import_suggested_clips.
internal.gotchas: The UI button is not yet shipped (follows in web-ui-v2). The endpoint processes up to 600 clips per call, 4 at a time. Clips that already exist for the same window (±0.5 s) and size are skipped. Audit event media.clip.created is only written when at least one clip is queued.
internal.talk_track: Instead of clicking render for each clip and each size separately — which for a 110-session event means 220+ clicks — you can now fire one API call or ask your AI assistant to render every suggested clip in every size with your brand kit applied automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The Clips guide should document the render-suggested endpoints (recording and import variants), the dryRun parameter, the per-size deduplication behaviour, and the brand-kit application logic.
draft.why_use_it: Clips let you turn the best moments from your session recordings into short, branded video assets ready for social media and advocacy campaigns. The suggested-clip engine identifies the most compelling windows in each recording and renders them with your brand kit — logo, colors and captions — in every aspect ratio your channels require. Use Clips after an event to build a library of shareable content without manually editing video.

entries.title: Agent events: Cvent registration link follows the event mapping
entries.summary: When an event is mapped to a Cvent event through the Apps engine, the registration link on the agent event card, the **`/r/`** redirect, the agenda, `llms.txt`, `agenda.md`, `mcp.json` and `snippet.js` now all point to the mapped Cvent event's own registration URL instead of the typed fallback URL. Events with a Cvent mapping no longer need a manually typed registration URL.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable agent events; then the agent event card and /r/ redirect use the mapped Cvent registration link automatically

where.path: Agent event card → registration link; /agent-events/r/<token> redirect

entries.use_case: Organizers using Cvent for registration no longer need to manually copy a registration URL into Sessionboard — the agent event surfaces the correct Cvent registration link automatically from the mapping. Attendees clicking the registration link from an AI assistant or event card are sent to the right Cvent event.

cs_action.note: Fix is automatic for any event with a Cvent mapping and attendee pull enabled. No action needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that their agent event card or /r/ redirect was sending attendees to the wrong Cvent registration page.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using agent events with a Cvent integration mapped via the Apps engine.
internal.staff_path: Apps → Cvent → Map Events; the mapped event's registration link is now read from GET /events/{id} on Cvent and cached for 15 min.
internal.gotchas: The fix requires the Cvent mapping to have attendee pull enabled (resolvePartnerConnection). Without it, the typed URL is used as a fallback. The mapped URL must be https on cvent.com or cvent.me — other hosts are rejected and fall back to the typed URL.
internal.talk_track: If you have Cvent mapped in Apps, your agent event card and registration redirect now automatically use the correct Cvent registration link — no need to paste a URL by hand.

draft.docs_gap: The Cvent integration guide should document that the agent event registration link is automatically sourced from the mapped Cvent event when attendee pull is enabled, and that a manually typed registration URL is only used as a fallback.
draft.why_use_it: Agent events expose your event's key details — including the registration link — to AI assistants, event cards and public artifacts like the agenda and MCP feed. When your event is connected to Cvent, the registration link is read directly from the mapped Cvent event so attendees always land on the right registration page without any manual URL entry.

entries.title: Agent sites: tour collection routes now resolve correctly (no more 404 on stop pages)
entries.summary: Pages on agent sites that are bound to a **tour** collection (e.g. `/labs/{slug}`) now load correctly instead of returning a 404. The fix resolves a mismatch between the `tour:` prefix stored in a tour's ID and the `series:` prefix used when looking up collection events, so every stop page — including its request-a-seat form — renders as expected.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable agent sites; then sites.sessionboard.com/p/<your-slug>

where.path: sites.sessionboard.com/p/<slug> — agent site pages bound to a tour collection

entries.use_case: Organizers running a multi-city tour (e.g. an event content lab with stops in different cities) can publish an agent site where each stop has its own page. Visitors navigating to a stop's URL now land on the correct page with its registration or request-a-seat form instead of hitting a 404.

cs_action.note: Fix is automatic on deploy; no customer action required. Affects any agent site with a collection route bound to a tour created via make_tour (IDs prefixed tour:).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that individual stop pages on a tour-based agent site return 404, or when setting up a new multi-stop tour site.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with agent sites enabled who use the tour/series feature to publish multi-stop event pages.
internal.staff_path: sites.sessionboard.com/p/<slug>/<collection-path>/<stop-slug> — verify the stop page loads after deploy.
internal.gotchas: The bug only affected tours created via make_tour whose IDs carry the tour: prefix. Tours bound by name (as in local dev) were unaffected. Also fixes the route path reported by preview_site / get_site (now /labs/{slug} instead of /labs-item).

draft.docs_gap: The site-builder guide should document how to bind a collection route to a tour, including the tour ID format and how stop pages are resolved from the collection URL.

entries.title: Marketing shows API: name validation, timezone enforcement, safe schedule updates, and dead-link warnings on AI-built pages
entries.summary: The Marketing shows API now rejects blank or whitespace-only **Name** values with a clear 400 error instead of a server error or silent save, and trims leading/trailing spaces from valid names. **Timezone** must be a valid IANA zone (e.g. `America/New_York`); invalid strings are rejected. Partial **Schedule** updates (via `PUT`) now merge into the stored schedule rather than wiping unset keys — sending only `timezone` no longer clears `weekday`, `time` or `duration`. The `check_page_html` and `write_page_html` MCP tools now emit a `link.dead` warning for placeholder `href="#"`, empty `href`, or `#id` anchors with no matching element on the page.

where.path: Marketing → Shows (API: /marketing/org/:orgId/shows and /v1/marketing/shows; MCP: create_show / update_show / check_page_html / write_page_html)

entries.use_case: Teams managing shows via the API or an AI assistant no longer risk creating shows with blank names or invalid timezones, and partial schedule edits (e.g. changing only the timezone) no longer accidentally clear the day, time or duration. AI-built event pages are now flagged when they contain dead links before they go live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that a show's schedule was unexpectedly cleared after an API update, or that a blank show name caused a server error, or that an AI-built page shipped with broken anchor links.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Marketing shows API or MCP tools (create_show / update_show) to manage shows programmatically.
internal.gotchas: The schedule merge behaviour is a breaking fix for anyone who was relying on sending a partial schedule object to clear fields — they must now explicitly send null for a key to clear it.

draft.docs_gap: The run-a-weekly-show guide should document the API/MCP schedule object structure (weekday 0–6 = Sunday–Saturday, timezone must be IANA, null clears a key) and note that blank names are rejected.
draft.why_use_it: The Marketing shows API lets you create and manage recurring shows — including their schedule, episodes and guest bookings — programmatically or through an AI assistant. Consistent validation means the data you store is always clean and complete, so downstream surfaces like show pages and podcast feeds reflect exactly what you intended.

entries.title: RSVP manage page shows Brand Kit; AI assistants can apply an email design in one step
entries.summary: The **Change or withdraw your request** page (linked from event emails) now inherits the event's **Brand Kit** — logo, colours and fonts — so participants see a consistent branded experience. Separately, AI assistants using the MCP server can now pass `apply: true` when proposing an email design, which proposes and accepts the design in a single call instead of requiring a manual approval step in **Event → Emails**.

where.path: Event → Emails (email design); registration manage link (/rsvp/:token) for participants

entries.use_case: Organizers using an AI assistant to restyle event emails no longer need to manually accept each design change in the admin — the assistant can apply it directly. Participants who follow the manage-registration link in an email now see the event's brand instead of an unbranded page.

cs_action.note: Both changes are additive and default-on. The apply:true path is MCP-only; organizers not using an AI assistant are unaffected. Orgs with the assistant_approvals feature flag keep the proposal-only behaviour — the assistant's answer will say applied: false with a note.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer is using Claude or ChatGPT to manage email designs and finds the extra approval step in the admin tedious, or when they notice the RSVP manage page looks unbranded.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the MCP server to manage event emails, or any customer whose participants use the RSVP manage link.
internal.staff_path: MCP: update_event_email_draft with apply: true. RSVP page: /rsvp/:token — brand is returned automatically when a Brand Kit is assigned to the event or org.
internal.gotchas: Orgs with the assistant_approvals feature flag will NOT have designs auto-applied even when apply: true is passed — the response returns applied: false and an applied_note explaining why. The previous design is kept in history and is restorable.

draft.docs_gap: The automated-emails guide should document the apply:true MCP parameter for update_event_email_draft, the assistant_approvals gate, and the fact that the /rsvp manage page now renders the event's Brand Kit.
draft.why_use_it: Automated emails keep participants informed at every stage of their registration or submission journey. Pairing those emails with a consistent brand — carried through to the linked manage page — reinforces trust and reduces confusion. When an AI assistant helps you restyle emails, the apply-in-one-call behaviour means the assistant's approved design goes live immediately, keeping your workflow moving without extra clicks.

entries.title: Set a unique social share image for each page path on a Site
entries.summary: Each route path on an agent-built Site can now have its own **share image**, so individual pages (for example, `/labs/quantum-lab` vs `/labs/bio-lab`) unfurl with distinct cards on LinkedIn and Slack instead of all showing the same image. A path-level image overrides both the page's **head share image** and the Site-wide share image. Set it via the `edit_site` tool's `share.set` operation or the `site_share_image` agent output destination; clear it by passing `null`.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable agent sites; then use the edit_site tool's share.set operation or the site_share_image agent output destination

where.path: sites.sessionboard.com/p/<slug> — per-path share image set via Ask or the edit_site tool

entries.use_case: When a single collection route (like `/labs/{slug}`) renders many distinct pages, each lab or item can now show its own branded card when shared on LinkedIn or Slack — instead of every link unfurling with the same generic image. Useful for tour sites, product showcases, or any site where one URL template serves multiple unique pieces of content.

cs_action.note: Per-path share images are set via the edit_site MCP tool (share.set op) or the site_share_image agent output destination. The write_output destination path parameter requires a follow-up one-line zod addition in the MCP server before it is reachable from MCP — confirm that follow-up has shipped before telling customers to use it from an AI assistant.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using agent sites has a collection route (e.g. /labs/{slug}, /speakers/{slug}) and complains that all pages share the same og:image when posted to LinkedIn or Slack.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with agent sites enabled who publish collection-style pages where each item should have a distinct social card.
internal.staff_path: edit_site tool → share.set { path: '/labs/quantum-lab', imageUrl: 'https://…' }; or agent output destination site_share_image with optional path.
internal.gotchas: Template paths like {slug} and http URLs are refused. Max 500 paths per site. The write_output destination path param needs a follow-up MCP server change to be callable from Claude/ChatGPT — check before demoing.
internal.talk_track: If you have a site where one URL pattern serves many different pages — like a lab directory or a speaker roster — you can now give each page its own share image so every LinkedIn post looks distinct.

draft.docs_gap: The site-builder guide should document the share image priority order (path > page > site), the edit_site share.set operation syntax, the site_share_image output destination, path normalisation rules, and the 500-path limit.
draft.why_use_it: The Site builder lets you publish fully branded public pages for your event, program or content without writing code. When a single route template serves many distinct pages — speaker profiles, lab pages, product showcases — per-path share images ensure each page presents its own card when someone shares a link on LinkedIn or Slack, giving every piece of content its own identity in social feeds. Images are set through Ask or the agent output pipeline and resolve in priority order: path-level first, then page-level, then site-wide.

entries.title: RSVP management page shows the event's Brand Kit header
entries.summary: The **Change or withdraw your request** page (reached from registration emails) now displays a full-width branded header in the event's accent colour, with the light logo linked to the event page and an **Event page** link. The header uses the Brand Kit's fonts and contrast-safe text colours. Pages for events without a Brand Kit are unchanged.

where.path: Registration email → Change or withdraw your request → RSVP management page

entries.use_case: When a registrant clicks "Change or withdraw your request" in a branded registration email, they now land on a page that matches the event's look and feel — same colours, logo and fonts — instead of a bare, unbranded page that felt like a different product.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why their RSVP management page looks unbranded compared to their registration emails, or when onboarding a customer who cares about end-to-end brand consistency.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using registration emails who has a Brand Kit configured — the improvement is automatic.
internal.gotchas: The branded header only appears when the event has a Brand Kit applied. Events without a kit continue to show the old small event logo. The kit must be set via the Brand Kits settings or the MCP update_brand_kit tool.
internal.talk_track: Your registrants now see a fully branded page when they manage their RSVP — same colours, logo and fonts as the email that brought them there. No extra setup needed if you already have a Brand Kit on the event.

draft.docs_gap: The brand-kits guide should note that the RSVP management page (/rsvp/:token) is one of the surfaces that inherits the Brand Kit, including the accent-colour header band, light logo and heading/body fonts.
draft.why_use_it: Brand Kits let you define your event's colours, logo and typography once and apply them consistently across emails, portals and public-facing pages. When a registrant follows a link from a registration email, they see the same branding they expect — reinforcing trust and keeping the experience cohesive from inbox to action. Setting up a kit takes only a few minutes and automatically flows through to every surface that supports it.
problems: src/data/release-notes/2026-11-18.json [rsvp-brand-kit-band] where.path is required — the menu path where the change shows up

entries.title: Media History: Activity tab and counted downloads
entries.summary: **Media → History** now has two tabs: **Imports and sends** (the existing table) and **Activity**, which lists who downloaded, edited, or imported each file — filterable by All / Downloads / Edits / Imports, with load-more paging and deep-link support via `?tab=activity`. Download buttons across **Clips**, **ClipExportMenu**, **MediaChaptersClips** and **AudioMediaLayout** now route through a secure link request that writes a **Downloaded** row to the Activity log; buttons are disabled while the link is fetched and show an error toast on failure. History filters also gain **Media** and **Media import** subject types (in English, French, German and Spanish).

where.path: Marketing → Media → History → Activity

entries.use_case: Teams that share recordings and clips with speakers or partners can now see exactly who downloaded which file and when, making it easy to confirm delivery, audit access, and follow up with anyone who hasn't retrieved their content yet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to confirm that a speaker or partner actually downloaded their clip or recording, or when they need an audit trail of who accessed media files.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Media or Clips who distributes recordings to speakers, sponsors or partners and needs accountability over file access.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → History → Activity tab; deep-link with ?tab=activity
internal.gotchas: Download tracking only applies to org-staff download paths (Clips toolbar, ClipExportMenu, MediaChaptersClips, AudioMediaLayout). Speaker Portal and magic-link viewers (ClipPreviewModal, SpeakerClipsGallery) are intentionally excluded because they have no org staff token. Client-built VTT downloads are also not tracked. Event-only staff see only rows scoped to their events.
internal.talk_track: You can now open Media → History → Activity and see a timestamped list of every download, edit and import — who did it, on which file, and when. It's the audit trail your team has been asking for.

draft.docs_gap: The media-library guide should document the new Activity tab, its filters (All / Downloads / Edits / Imports), load-more paging, the ?tab=activity deep-link, and the fact that download buttons now write a Downloaded row to the log.
draft.why_use_it: The Media library is where your team stores, organises and distributes recordings, clips and audio files produced from your event. The Activity tab gives you a full audit trail of every download, edit and import against each media item, so you always know who has accessed your content and can trace any unexpected activity. Download tracking is built into every clip and recording export button, so the log fills automatically without any extra steps from your team.

entries.title: Media: downloads, imports and clip actions now appear in org and event History
entries.summary: Media activity — including file **downloads**, **import** lifecycle events (started, completed, per-file results, canceled, retried), **clip edits**, **branded renders**, **transcript exports** and **Descript sends** — now appears in org and event **History**. A new **Media → Activity** feed lets staff filter by item, import, actor, operation or date range, and is also available via the MCP `list_media_activity` tool. Downloads are issued through a dedicated endpoint that returns a 15-minute presigned link and logs the action at the moment the link is handed out.

where.path: Marketing → Media → Activity (per-library feed); org or event History (audit trail)

entries.use_case: When a speaker or executive says they downloaded a clip or browsed the media library, you can now look up exactly what they did and when — including which file was downloaded, who started an import, and whether individual files succeeded or were skipped as duplicates. This is especially useful for post-event accountability and troubleshooting stalled imports.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why they cannot tell what a speaker or stakeholder did with their media, or when an import produced unexpected results and they need to trace what happened.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Media add-on or Marketing Media feature who needs accountability over content downloads and imports.
internal.staff_path: Org or event History → filter subject = media_item or media_import; or Marketing → Media → Activity tab.
internal.gotchas: Download audit rows are written when the presigned link is issued, not when S3 delivers the file — so a row appears even if the person closed the tab before the download finished. The companion UI PR (web-ui-v2) that switches Download buttons to the new endpoint and surfaces the Activity list in Media → History is not yet merged; until it lands, the activity feed is accessible via the API/MCP only and History rows appear but the in-product Activity tab may not be visible.
internal.talk_track: Before this change, Media wrote almost nothing readable to History — now every download, import and clip action is a named, searchable row. If a speaker or executive asks 'did they actually watch/download my session?', you can look it up in seconds.

draft.docs_gap: The media-library guide should document the new Activity feed (filters, scoping rules for event-only vs portfolio-scoped staff), the download endpoint behaviour (presigned link, 15-minute expiry, audit on link issuance), and the full list of audited operations (downloaded, import lifecycle, clip edited, clip rendered, transcript exported, sent to Descript).
draft.why_use_it: The Media library centralises recordings, clips, transcripts and branded renders for your event. The activity feed and History integration give your team a complete, searchable record of every meaningful action taken on that content — who downloaded what, which imports ran and how each file resolved — so you can answer questions from speakers, executives or your own team without guesswork.

entries.title: Agenda Conflicts tab: clearer copy, confirm-before-delete, and accessibility fixes on the rules panel
entries.summary: The **Conflicts** tab's rules panel has been updated with clearer labels and safer interactions. The summary bar now reads "1 warning" (not "1 warnings"), column hints show counts like "2 rules · blocks the agenda", and the saved-rules list is headed **Saved rules** instead of repeating "Your rules". Deleting a rule now opens a confirmation dialog that also points to the on/off switch for pausing instead. **Generate recommendations** is renamed **Generate ideas** and is disabled while generating; **Re-check** shows **Checking…** while running. The `Ctrl ↵` keyboard shortcut in the composer reflects the user's OS (Windows/Linux vs Mac). Info icons on rule cards are now focusable buttons, the delete button is always visible at 28 px, and contrast on "Try instead" and "Added" labels meets WCAG 2.2 AA.

where.path: Sessions → Agenda → Conflicts tab → Conflict rules panel

entries.use_case: Organizers managing scheduling conflicts can now delete rules with confidence thanks to a confirmation step, and the renamed "Generate ideas" button and corrected grammar make the panel easier to read and use at a glance.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about scheduling conflict detection or mentions the Conflicts tab feeling confusing or hard to use with a keyboard or screen reader.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer using the agenda Conflicts tab to manage scheduling rules.
internal.staff_path: Sessions → Agenda → Conflicts tab
internal.gotchas: The PR author noted they had not verified the changes in a browser before merging (local session didn't load a user), so a quick smoke-test in staging is advisable before highlighting to customers.
internal.talk_track: The rules panel now has clearer labels, a safer delete flow, and passes WCAG 2.2 AA contrast — good to mention to customers who have raised accessibility requirements.

draft.docs_gap: The agenda guide's Conflicts section should document the rules panel columns (blocks the agenda vs flags only vs edit here), the confirm-before-delete dialog, the Generate ideas / Checking… states, and the Saved rules list label.
draft.why_use_it: The Conflicts tab lets you define and enforce scheduling rules — such as blocking double-booked speakers or flagging back-to-back sessions — directly on the agenda. Rules are grouped by severity so you can see at a glance which conflicts stop the agenda from publishing and which are advisory only. Generating ideas surfaces rule suggestions based on your program, and the on/off switch on each rule lets you pause enforcement without losing your configuration.

entries.title: Reviewer scoring sidebar is wider on large monitors
entries.summary: On the submission review page, the scoring sidebar now expands on wider screens: **352 px** at xl (1280–1535 px) and **416 px** at 2xl (1536 px+), up from a fixed 288 px at all sizes. Scoring questions and help text no longer wrap every few words on large monitors.

where.path: Evaluations → [plan] → Submission detail — scoring sidebar

entries.use_case: Reviewers working on large monitors can now read scoring questions and help text without awkward line breaks, making it faster to score submissions without losing context.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a reviewer or organizer mentions that the scoring panel feels cramped or hard to read on a large screen.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event using review plans with scorecards; benefit is most visible on 1280 px+ displays.
internal.gotchas: No change below lg (1024 px); the fix is CSS-only and ships automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the scoring sidebar width adapts to the viewport on xl and 2xl screens.

entries.title: Sponsor Scout: search a global sponsor catalog and add companies to your pipeline
entries.summary: A new **Sponsor Search** page under **Advanced Search** lets organizers search a continuously updated catalog of potential event sponsors, filter by industry, tier, region and CRM status, and add any company directly to the sponsor pipeline with one click.

where.path: Advanced Search → Sponsor Search

entries.use_case: Event teams looking for new sponsors can search a pre-populated catalog of companies that have sponsored similar events, filter by tier and region, see whether a company is already in their CRM, and push promising leads straight into the sponsor pipeline — without leaving Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: The background Sponsor Scout agent runs on prod-us only and is enabled by default (ENABLE_SPONSOR_SCOUT_AGENT=true). The catalog is seeded from 90 topic/region cells; a full-budget run against the dev cluster has not yet been verified. Confirm catalog has sufficient coverage before promoting to customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to find new sponsors or says their sponsorship pipeline is thin going into a new event cycle.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizers on prod-us who have the advanced_search feature and use the sponsor pipeline; not yet available on EU or ME.
internal.staff_path: Advanced Search → Sponsor Search
internal.gotchas: Sponsor Scout agent is prod-us only at launch; EU and ME customers will not see catalog results. The catalog is built incrementally — early runs may have limited coverage for niche topics. The add-to-pipeline flow reuses the Speaker Prospect promote path; a regression fix in this PR ensures it links to a pre-set account_id rather than deduping by name.
internal.talk_track: Instead of researching sponsors manually, your team can search a catalog of companies that have sponsored events like yours, see which ones are already in your CRM, and add the best fits to your pipeline in one click.

draft.docs_gap: The Advanced Search guide covers contact/speaker search but does not yet document the Sponsor Search page, its filters (industry, tier, region, CRM status), or the add-to-pipeline action; a new section or companion guide is needed.
draft.why_use_it: Finding sponsors typically means hours of manual research across conference websites and LinkedIn. Sponsor Search gives you a searchable catalog of companies that have sponsored events in your topic area, enriched with tier, industry and region data. Filter the list to the companies that fit your event, check their existing CRM status at a glance, and add them to your pipeline in one step so your team can start working them immediately.

entries.title: Automations: filter rows now show "and" between them, with a plain-language hint
entries.summary: In the **Only enroll when** trigger filter and the **Assign reviewers** step's submission filters, a small **and** divider now appears between each filter row so it is clear that a record must match every condition. The enrollment hint text also updates to read: *A record must match every filter. To accept any of several values, pick them all in one filter.*

where.path: Automations → [automation] → Only enroll when / Assign reviewers → filters

entries.use_case: Organizers who build multi-condition automation triggers can now see at a glance that all filters must be satisfied — no more guessing whether conditions are AND or OR. The updated hint also explains how to handle OR logic (pick multiple values in a single filter).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks whether automation filters are AND or OR, or when they report that an automation is firing on records they did not expect.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using multi-condition automation triggers, especially those who have asked about filter logic.
internal.staff_path: Automations → open any automation → Only enroll when section or Assign reviewers step → add two or more filters
internal.gotchas: The joinLabel prop is opt-in; only the enrollment trigger and the Assign reviewers submission filters show the divider. Other screens that use FiltersBuilder are unchanged.
internal.talk_track: Multiple filters in an automation now show 'and' between each row, so it is obvious that every condition must match. If you need OR logic, add all the acceptable values inside a single filter row.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a short section explaining that multiple filters combine with AND logic, how the 'and' divider works, and how to achieve OR behaviour by selecting multiple values within one filter.
draft.why_use_it: Automations let you trigger actions — like enrolling a contact or assigning a reviewer — only when a record meets specific conditions. Stacking multiple filters lets you target exactly the right records without writing any code. The filter builder shows each condition as a row, and the "and" dividers make the logic explicit so you can build with confidence.
